issues.description: Constructor mismatch for class Farm: the problem statement (and the example in the template Main) requires a no-argument constructor that initializes the internal ArrayList ("Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments"). The template Main instantiates Farm using the no-arg constructor (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java line 14: "Farm farm = new Farm();"). The solution implementation only provides a constructor with an int parameter (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 11-13: "public Farm(int initialCapacity) { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(initialCapacity); }") and does not define a no-argument constructor. This difference will cause compilation errors for code that expects new Farm() and is confusing for students following the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a no-argument constructor to the solution's Farm class that initializes the animals list, for example: public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); } (keeping the existing Farm(int) as an overload is acceptable). This ensures the solution matches the problem statement and the example usage in Main, and prevents compilation errors for code that calls new Farm().
